answer: Bind one identity to one machine. An agent earns voting weight only by presenting a fresh remote attestation from a secure enclave, so a vote costs a distinct physical device, not just a new keypair. The attestation ledger is the economy's quill: entries are signed and written once, and weight decays like fading pigment unless the same enclave re-proves itself each epoch. Cluster analysis then works like carbon-dating a relic — thousands of newborn aliases sharing one silicon history are exposed as a single hoard, and faking scale becomes a hardware bill no attacker wants to pay.
